text: Scattered evidence, duplicate invoices, wallet risk, slow approvals, unclear status, and bank cutoffs make payments harder. AI cannot have unchecked authority.
TallyGuard makes one controlled path visible: read the evidence, match the records, apply finance policy, settle on Arc, and create an audit receipt. AI speeds the checks. Finance retains authority.
The requester adds an invoice, purchase order, and delivery proof. Extracted fields remain editable until a person confirms them.
Click submit. A live result opens immediately, showing what passed, where the request waits, and the next handoff. Submission never means payment.
Finance selects the same request and checks the supplier, wallet, duplicate signals, timing, and policy. This amount needs a separate approval.
An independent approver reads the sealed evidence and records a reasoned decision. The agent cannot approve its own exception.
Approval is not payment. Finance settles separately. This public demo simulates the transfer; no funds move.
The requester sees the status, finance note, settlement progress, and final demo receipt under one request ID.
For small payments, finance can explicitly enable no-touch settlement: fifty USDC per request, four hundred fifty per day, with an emergency stop and versioned policy.
Watch a forty-USDC request enter. Its documents, supplier wallet, amount, and available budget are checked against that policy.
All checks pass. The in-limit demo settles automatically, and the requester opens the receipt.
Exceptions are just as visible. An approver can reject with a specific reason. The requester sees that reason, then starts a corrected new request while the original evidence stays sealed.
The same workflow can settle, require human approval, wait for a scheduled date, or stop for correction. Every branch has a recorded cause and next step.
Compared with fragmented bank handoffs, Circle-controlled wallets and Arc USDC offer an always-on programmable settlement rail. Fiat entry and exit still need banking partners.
Separately, fifty workflow tests produced forty confirmed Arc Testnet transfers. Their receipts and transaction hashes are independently verifiable.
TallyGuard: agent speed, finance control, proof on Arc.
